 CORAM:HONOURABLE MS. JUSTICE VAIBHAVI D. NANAVATI  Date : 04/05/2023  ORAL ORDER 1.

Heard Mr. Chirag Parekh, learned advocate appearing for the petitioners, Mr. Niraj Sharma,
learned AGP for respondent No.1 and Mr. Kaushal Pandya, learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2.
2.

By way of present petition, the petitioners herein are a group of persons carrying business of selling live poultry and mutton slaughtered in government dedicated slaughter house since past 20-25 years in the Ved Road area in Surat.

It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioners are in receipt of valid licence issued by respondent Nos 2 to 4 vide various certificates to carry on the business of poultry selling and selling slaughtered mutton.

The petitioner has placed reliance on the said C/SCA/2560/2023 ORDER DATED: 04/05/2023 licence, which is produced at Annexure "B"
(Colly).

sentences.text: 4. Learned advocates appearing for the respective parties have jointly submitted that the reliefs prayed for by the petitioners would be governed by the order dated 11.4.2023 passed by the Division Bench in Civil Application (For Direction) No.10 of 2023 in Writ Petition (PIL) No. 133 of 2021 and connected Civil Applications.

At this stage, it is apposite to refer to the operative part of the said order passed by the Division Bench in Civil Application (For Direction) No.10 of 2023 in Writ Petition (PIL) No. 133 of 2021 and connected Civil Applications dated 11.4.2023, wherein Para-6 reads thus:
"6. All the meat shops and slaughter houses which are closed by the authorities for the reason that they have failed to comply with the licencing and regulatory norms,
food and safety standards, pollution control requirements and for any such other legal considerations including non-observance of hygiene imperatives, could hardly be permitted to be reopened on spacious grounds, unless they become fully C/SCA/2560/2023 ORDER DATED: 04/05/2023 compliant of such norms and regulations.
Intervention is not called for by the court when it comes to abiding by the food safety etc. norms.
It would be an overriding principle that the public concerns of hygiene and food safety will have to prevail.
6.1 The details and figures furnished by the State Authorities in their affidavit-in-replies, which have been noted in above, do suggest that the authorities have acted pragmatic.
All slaughter houses and meat shops are not ordered to be closed.
Those who are norms compliant, are permitted to run their business.

Even the shops and premises owners who are given the show cause notice or whose shops are ordered to be closed, could meet with the requirements of law and after fulfilling the norms, may approach the competent authority or competent committee seeking to reopen their business premises or shops.
The State Slaughter Committee and District Level Committees are functional.

6.2 For all the forgoing reasons, except granting prayer in Civil Application No.11 of 2023, allowing the applicants thereof to join as parties in the main Writ Petition (PIL), no relief in rest of the Civil Applications could be granted.

6.3 It is however,
observed that it will be open for any meat shop owner, meat vendor or slaughter house owner to approach the competent authority or competent committee by showing that it has ensured compliance of all the laws and regulations as may be applicable.

In all such cases, it is provided, the competent authority or the State or District Level Committee as the case may be, shall permit the shop or slaughter house to be reopened, permitting the owner or C/SCA/2560/2023 ORDER DATED:
04/05/2023 vendor to run the business by continuing to comply with the business norms. 6.4
It is also observed that if any such application is made by any shop owner or vendor, it shall be dealt with expeditiously without booking delay."

Considering the facts being undisputed, the order passed in the Civil Application (For Direction)
No.10 of 2023 in Writ Petition (PIL) No. 133 of 2021 and connected Civil Applications dated 11.4.2023 shall govern the present petition.

The petitioners herein shall comply with the direction as directed by the Division Bench in Para-6 of the order dated 11.4.2023 passed in Civil Application (For Direction) No.10 of 2023 in Writ Petition (PIL) No. 133 of 2021 and connected Civil Applications.
6. With the aforesaid direction, the present petition is disposed of with consent of learned advocate appearing for the respective parties.
This Court has otherwise not opined on the merits of the matter.
